title: TypeNet: Deep Learning Keystroke Biometrics
objective: Investigates LSTM networks for keystroke biometric authentication in free-text scenarios, comparing three learning approaches (softmax, contrastive, triplet loss) and evaluating performance across physical/touchscreen keyboards.
methodology: LSTM-based deep learning models trained with keystroke sequences, evaluated using different loss functions, sample sizes, and device types (physical vs touchscreen keyboards).
dataset: Largest free-text keystroke databases with >136M keystrokes from 168,000 physical keyboard users and 60,000 touchscreen users.
performance: TypeNet achieves 2.2% EER for physical keyboards and 9.2% for touchscreen keyboards, with scalable performance up to 100,000 users.
limitations: Performance degrades with very large user counts; device-specific behavior may affect accuracy.

title: Covert lie detection using keyboard dynamics
objective: Detecting fake identities without external verification (documents, biometrics) in security and online contexts.
methodology: Keystroke dynamics analysis using unexpected questions to reveal deception clues through typing pattern deviations.
dataset: 60 participants (40 training, 20 test) with fabricated ID profiles and real personal information.
performance: Achieved 95% accuracy in distinguishing liars from truth-tellers using keystroke dynamics.
limitations: Requires predefined questions; generalizability to real-world scenarios may be limited.

title: Non-Acted Text and Keystrokes Database and Learning Methods to Recognize Emotions
objective: Develop a multimodal text-keystrokes dataset and learning methods for emotion recognition through feature fusion and SVM-based classification.
methodology: Collected text-keystroke data from 69 participants using controlled video stimuli. Extracted and fused text and keystroke features using tree-based selection and SVM for emotion classification.
dataset: Multimodal text-keystrokes dataset with 69 participants, including video-induced stimuli and unguided text reviews.
performance: Achieved 86.95% accuracy in emotion classification via text-keystroke fusion; 100% accuracy for pleasure-displeasure classes using SVM and feature fusion.
limitations: Data collected in controlled environments may lack real-world variability; limited to predefined emotion classes.

title: NOT MENTIONED
objective: Explore emotional influences on keystroke dynamics due to limited prior research on emotion-induced variance in keyboard typing patterns.
methodology: Controlled experiment using International Affective Digitized Sounds (IADS) to induce emotional states, followed by two-way ANOVA analysis of keystroke data.
dataset: Keystroke data collected from 52 participants under IADS-induced emotional conditions (Valence x Arousal dimensions).
performance: Arousal significantly affected duration (p < .05) and latency (p < .01), but not accuracy. Emotional effects were smaller than individual variability.
limitations: Small emotional effect size and potential methodological limitations in parameter specificity.

title: DeepMood: Modeling Mobile Phone Typing Dynamics for Mood Detection
objective: Detect mood disturbances and severity using mobile phone typing dynamics metadata, offering non-intrusive mental health monitoring in daily life settings.
methodology: Proposes DeepMood, a late fusion deep architecture combining RNNs for multi-view metadata (keypress timing, accelerometer) with interaction modeling across views.
dataset: BiAffect study data from 20 participants (7 bipolar I, 5 bipolar II, 8 controls) with session-level typing metadata and clinical ratings (HDRS/YMRS).
performance: Achieved 90.31% depression score prediction accuracy using session-level typing dynamics (typically <1 minute), demonstrating feasibility of metadata-driven mood inference.
limitations: Privacy constraints limit character data collection; reliance on self-reported clinical ratings may introduce bias; requires further validation on diverse populations.
